standard_prerequisites.name: A module annihilated by the ideal is a module over the quotient, and tensoring it over the quotient with the base changed quotient gives back the module when the quotients agree
standard_prerequisites.use: Proves the base case of the induction, which is the heart of the equivalence.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness of the ring map makes the tensor product with it exact, so a short exact sequence of modules gives a short exact sequence after tensoring
standard_prerequisites.use: Carries the induction step from the submodule and the quotient to the whole module.

standard_prerequisites.name: A power torsion module is the union of the submodules annihilated by the successive powers of the ideal, and tensor products commute with colimits
standard_prerequisites.use: Passes from the modules annihilated by a fixed power to an arbitrary power torsion module.

core_obligations: Record that one implication is immediate, and prove the other: assume that the quotient map is an isomorphism and show that the natural map from every power torsion module to its base change is an isomorphism (proof lines 24275-24279).

Base case: for a module annihilated by the ideal, identify its base change with the tensor product over the quotient of the base changed quotient, and use the assumption to get back the module (proof lines 24279-24284).

Induction step: for a module annihilated by a higher power, display the short exact sequence with the submodule annihilated by the previous power and the quotient, tensor it using flatness of the ring map, and apply the induction hypothesis to the two outer terms to conclude for the middle one (proof lines 24286-24293).

General case: write a power torsion module as the union of the submodules annihilated by the successive powers, and conclude using that tensor products commute with colimits (proof lines 24294-24297).
proof_roadmap: One implication is immediate; for the other, start with the case of a module annihilated by the ideal (proof lines 24275-24284).
Induct on the power of the ideal using the short exact sequence and flatness (proof lines 24286-24293).
Finish for an arbitrary power torsion module by expressing it as a union and using commutation with colimits (proof lines 24294-24297).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a pair satisfying the equivalent conditions of the preceding characterization of flatness on torsion, the natural map from every power torsion module to its base change is an isomorphism exactly when the quotient of the base by the ideal is isomorphic to the corresponding quotient of the target (statement lines 24263-24273). The proof is a two-stage induction: the case of a module annihilated by the ideal is a direct computation over the quotient, and the general case of a module annihilated by a fixed power is handled by the displayed short exact sequence with flatness carrying the hypothesis on the outer terms to the middle, after which an arbitrary power torsion module is treated as the union of these and the conclusion follows from commutation of tensor products with colimits (proof lines 24275-24297). The induction with the outer terms is what makes the statement sharp. The counted statement depends on the preceding characterization, which is delivered as a context span so that its label resolves inside the package, and there is no further reference, so the card carries no navigation stub.
